title: The Work Between Moments
logline: A person or small crew works through a real, bounded task, something that must be made, repaired, prepared, moved or completed, and reality alone decides whether it succeeds. The film watches contact, recognition and adjustment happen in real time, and lets actions, natural sound and the participants' own words carry whatever can be known about what they felt.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From the echo that follows a single strike to a real task in progress, where contact, recognition and adjustment happen moment by moment.

thread_out.thread: The moment-by-moment rhythm of work becomes a rhythm taught aloud: a drumming teacher passing on, in spoken syllables, something too fast to watch.

requirements: An active, ethically filmable working environment where a bounded task unfolds through observable action
Sufficient visual and natural-sound variation without the crew interrupting or reshaping the work
Safe camera access and fully informed participant consent

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Every moment of real work, easy or hard, is made of the same few parts: something is touched, it feels a certain way, it is recognised, there is a push behind the next move, and attention points somewhere. A skilled worker's quick eye is partly recognition that has built up over time.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: වැඩ කරන සෑම මොහොතකම ස්පර්ශය, විඳීම, හඳුනාගැනීම, ඊළඟ පියවරට ඇති උත්සාහය සහ අවධානය යන එකම කොටස් ඇති අතර, පළපුරුදු ඇසක් යනු කාලයක් තිස්සේ ශක්තිමත් වූ හඳුනාගැනීමකි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches seven 'universal' mental factors that are present in every moment of mind without exception: contact, feeling, perception, volition, one-pointedness, the life-faculty and attention (C020). Perception recognises by marks and leaves a mark for recognising again, so that over time recognition grows firm, and volition is the effort behind every act, weak in the bare sensing moments and strong where action is done (C020). Feeling is present in every mind and is always pleasant, painful or neutral; the texts say there is no fourth way (C032).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film stays with one real task from beginning to end: hands, tools, checks, corrections and quiet intervals, in natural sound. Moments where something is touched, noticed, recognised or changed are left to play out, and any feeling is named only in the participants' own words, so the viewer assembles the parts of each moment without the film claiming to see inside anyone.

key_terms.en: volition: the effort in every act

lesson.caution: The seven factors are not a seven-step plot or a reading of anyone's inner life, and 'attention' here is not wellness-style mindfulness: the texts place it in angry and greedy moments too.
lesson.builds_on: The bell showed how long a single contact can echo; this film goes back inside one working moment and looks at the parts every such contact is made of.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
